question: Does the current Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes resolve the Pangasius hypophthalmus/Pangasianodon hypophthalmus conflict between the PAREX EIS station matrix and taxonomy table, and does that permit the EIS rows to be merged or counted as one verified fish record?

method.authority: California Academy of Sciences, Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes
method.authorityVersion: The indexed Catalog record identifies its online version as updated 2026-08-13. The official record excerpt was retrieved through bounded web search on 2026-11-24; opening the record directly returned HTTP 403.
method.query: Catalog record 56294 for the hypophthalmus name-group, URL https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=56294
method.interpretation: The Catalog documents both genus combinations as historical valid-as usages under the same nominal species record, and gives Pangasianodon hypophthalmus as current status. This supports a nomenclatural relationship between the printed combinations, not proof that the separate EIS rows refer to the same sampled organism, were correctly identified, or can be combined into a reliable count.

sourceCitation: RHR Consulting Services, Inc. (2022), PAREX Draft EIS Table 2-18 and Table 2-19; Revised EIS Tables 2-19 and 2-20; Fricke, R., Eschmeyer, W. N. & Van der Laan, R. (eds.), Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes, species record 56294, checked 2026-11-24.

stationMatrixLabel.sourceRole: Exact binomial string appearing in the Draft and Revised EIS station matrices.
stationMatrixLabel.catalogTreatment: The Catalog lists Pangasius hypophthalmus (Sauvage 1878) as a historical valid-as combination under its hypophthalmus record.

taxonomyTableLabel.sourceRole: Exact binomial string appearing in the Draft and Revised EIS taxonomic tables.
taxonomyTableLabel.catalogTreatment: The Catalog gives Pangasianodon hypophthalmus (Sauvage 1878) as current status under the same hypophthalmus record.

nameCrosswalk.boundedConclusion: A present-day taxonomic crosswalk may link the two strings as alternative historical/current generic combinations for the same nominal species. Preserve both verbatim in the source transcription and annotate the candidate relationship separately.

limitations: The Catalog's current name status does not authenticate either PAREX field identification or show that the two table rows derive from the same specimen or event.
The PAREX Draft and Revised EIS conflict on fish collection method and contain unreconciled table and narrative totals; the taxonomy cross-check does not correct those source inconsistencies.
No field sheets, specimen identifiers, vouchers, fish-specific coordinates, or written correction from the EIS preparer were reviewed for this cross-check.
The direct Catalog page request returned HTTP 403; conclusions are limited to the official indexed record excerpt.
No item-specific permission to redistribute the EIS-derived list or Catalog content was established.
decision: Keep Pangasius hypophthalmus and Pangasianodon hypophthalmus as distinct verbatim source strings in the EIS transcription. Record the Catalog-supported nomenclatural relationship only as a candidate name crosswalk; do not silently normalize either label, merge table rows, change the EIS's exact-string counts, claim a verified single biological species, add a species/occurrence/app row, or infer current presence. NCR and Luzon remain incomplete.
followUps: Seek a field log, specimen/voucher identifier, or written correction from the PAREX EIS preparer before treating the two table strings as one row or counting them as one source taxon.
Request specialist review if the source organism is ever considered for a species-level assertion.
Keep the parent EIS method conflict, station attribution, and source reuse questions open independently of this name cross-check.
